text:
This document goes deeper than the mechanics foundation on land, water and air transport in Rust: how each vehicle class is obtained, what fuels it, how it decays, and how 2026 updates changed it, especially the Naval Update's player-built boats and Deep Sea [2][3]. Boats are the best-documented area because Facepunch published detailed 2026 changelists for them [2][3][5].

Confidence is Medium. The 2026 boat, fuel and decay-change claims rest on Facepunch devblogs, but Facepunch's wiki pages for the older vehicles (minicopter, scrap helicopter) are placeholders [18][19]. Their base health, fuel burn and decay values therefore come from dated community sources (2019 and 2020) and are flagged as possibly stale [21][22].
title: Rust Vehicles

text:
- Player-built boats arrived with the Naval Update: place a Boat Building Station in water, then use a Boat Building Plan and boat blocks [2].
- Boat engines run on low grade fuel and burn it fast; sails, anchors, cannons, planks and ramps are the other parts [2].
- Shipshape (5 March 2026) raised the boat decay delay from 12 to 24 hours and cut decay duration from 18 to 12 hours; a boat counts as used only when steering input is received [3].
- The Boat Building Station crafts for 200 Wood and 1 Tarp at Workbench Level 1, and the Boat Building Plan for 20 Wood [11][12].
- At Bandit Camp the Air Wolf air-vehicle vendor will not sell until the helipad is repaired each wipe (Livestock, 1 Oct 2026) [1].
- The Deep Sea is reached by sailing toward the map edge in a strong boat; RHIBs can no longer enter it since 5 March 2026 [2][3].
- Horses need no fuel (they eat food) per a June 2026 community guide [20].
- Modular-car decay figures (about 8 hours outside, 36 inside) are from a 2020 community post and not re-verified on this build [21].
title: Rust Vehicles

title: Rust Vehicles

text:
**Evidence layer.**

## Water

- The first player-controlled vehicle was the powered rowboat (Vehicle Update, 5 April 2018): one driver plus three passengers, low grade fuel, a small bow storage box, and decay if left outside [10].
- Player-built boats (Naval Update, February 2026): build with a Boat Building Station placed in water, the Boat Building Plan and boat-specific blocks. Components are steering wheel (helm with a built-in lock and settable code), sails, engines, anchors, cannons, planks and ramps [2].
- Engines run on low grade fuel and burn it fast; engine and sail placement affects handling, and both can be reversed from the radial menu. Without an anchor a boat may drift to shore [2].
- Standard deployables can be placed on boats if they work on the Tugboat; Deploy and Edit mode places a Boat Building Station around an existing boat and is unavailable in the Deep Sea [2]. Tugboat spawns were disabled [2].
- Since 5 March 2026 electricity, industrial and water IO items work on boats; auto turrets, SAM sites, windmills, CCTV, seismic sensors, hanging lights and door controllers are blocked [3]. Repeated cannon hits can slow a player boat to 30% of maximum speed [3].
- Boats with flat bows take much more drag, and boat-shaped hulls are faster than box-shaped ones (May 2026) [5].
- The Deep Sea PT Boat is slower than the RHIB and uses more fuel but is stronger, with two turrets (dual .50 cal and single .50 cal) reloaded with 5.56 rifle ammo. Scientist-crewed RHIBs and PT Boats can be cleared and stolen [2].
- The kayak seats two and requires a Paddle [13]. A Small Boat Engine crafts from 50 Low Grade Fuel, 5 High Quality Metal and 2 Gears at Workbench Level 2 [14].

## Land

- Modular cars are assembled from a chassis plus modules; engine parts come in five types and three quality tiers (Low, Medium, High) [17]. Modules include engine, cockpit, passenger, storage, taxi, flatbed, camper and fuel tank variants [17].
- The Engine Vehicle Module crafts for 100 Metal Fragments and 3 High Quality Metal at Workbench Level 2 [15].
- Per the 2020 launch post: three chassis sizes, five engine parts required, higher part tiers make the car faster and more fuel efficient, and modules carry separate health [21]. A June 2026 guide gives module slots of small 2, medium 3, large 4 [20].
- Horses are claimed in a stable with a saddle (hold E and select Claim); the single saddle is not craftable [16]. Per a community guide horses are tamed in the wild or bought from a stable and need food, not fuel [20].

## Air

- Livestock (1 Oct 2026): the Bandit Camp Air Wolf helipad starts each wipe in disrepair and the vendor refuses sales until players repair it with hammer hits; it then stays repaired for the wipe [1].
- Minicopter costs 750 scrap and the scrap transport helicopter 1,250 scrap from the Air Wolf, or can be crafted from a blueprint, per a June 2026 community guide [20].
- The hot air balloon has an altimeter (April 2026) and armoured variants with staged armour loss (September 2026) [4][9].

## Fuel and decay

- Boat decay (Shipshape): delay 24 hours, then 12 hours of decay; a boat counts as used only with steering input [3]. The decay timer saves across restarts since September 2026 [9].
- Livestock added a Biofuel Generator that turns organic matter into low grade fuel, stirred by hand about every 30 minutes [1]. Dome crude pumps are covered under Version & Patch Notes [8][9].

text:
**Judgement layer.**

## Guidance 1 — Move or dock boats each session and recheck decay after restarts

- **Guidance:** Treat a player boat as safe from decay only for about a day of no steering input, then limited to 12 hours of decay, so move or dock it each session.
- **Evidence basis:** Decay delay and use definition [3]; timer persistence fix [9].
- **Confidence:** High. Primary Facepunch changelists, though numbers may be rebalanced.
- **So what:** Do not rely on an anchored, idle boat holding through a long absence.

## Guidance 2 — Do not trust pre-2026 community decay and fuel figures for cars and helicopters

- **Guidance:** Verify minicopter, scrap heli and car decay in game before planning around them.
- **Evidence basis:** Only 2019 and 2020 community sources give the numbers [21][22]; the wiki pages are placeholders [18][19].
- **Confidence:** Low. No primary source for current base values.
- **So what:** Admins and players should measure on their own server.

## Guidance 3 — Build boat hulls with a pointed bow

- **Guidance:** Prefer boat-shaped hulls over boxes for speed and fuel economy.
- **Evidence basis:** Drag changes [5]; engines burn fuel fast [2].
- **Confidence:** Medium. Direction is documented, magnitude is not.
- **So what:** A flat bow costs speed, and speed is the engine's main use for escape or pursuit.

## Guidance 4 — Expect air vehicle access to depend on repairing the Bandit Camp helipad

- **Guidance:** On default settings, plan a group repair of the Air Wolf pad early in the wipe before counting on purchased helicopters.
- **Evidence basis:** Repair rule [1]; prices from [20].
- **Confidence:** Medium. The mechanic is primary, prices are community.
- **So what:** Admins wanting instant access can set the convars named in [1].

title: Rust Wildlife and NPCs

text:
This deep-dive covers the non-player creatures of Rust: wild animals, the scientist and guard NPCs, the Bradley APC and Patrol Helicopter events, and the livestock introduced by the Livestock Update of 1 October 2026. It goes deeper than rust-game-mechanics-foundation, which only mentions hostile scientists at monuments.

Facepunch's Livestock post is the only primary source for the current build and it covers livestock, critters and NPC navigation, not health values or drop tables [1]. Health figures come from one community bestiary [4] and one hosting-company guide [5], neither tied to a stated build. Document confidence is therefore Low.
title: Rust Wildlife and NPCs

text:
- The Livestock Update (1 October 2026) adds cows and sheep that produce dung, milk and wool, can be bred, and can be sold to a Stable vendor [1].
- With the new navmesh enabled, NPCs can enter player structures and respect doors opening and closing [1].
- Only a subset of NPCs is processed each frame, so overload makes NPCs react slower rather than costing server FPS [1].
- The wiki Bradley Crate has 7 slots and always contains 1-4 MLRS Rockets (100%) [2].
- A community bestiary lists Bradley at 1000 health and scientists between 115 and 300 health depending on type (not build-stamped) [4].
- Wolves gather in groups of up to 3 and deer in packs of up to 5, per a June 2021 report [6].
- Patrol Helicopter health: the bestiary gives 9895.6 [4] while three other community sources say 10,000, with rotors about 900 and 500 [5][7]. No Facepunch page was found to settle it.
- Bradley health was 500 at its August 2017 launch [8] and is given as 1000 in 2024 and 2026 community sources, up from 500 [4][5][9].
title: Rust Wildlife and NPCs

text: Covered: wild animals, critters, livestock, scientist and guard NPCs, Bradley APC and Patrol Helicopter. Health and drops appear only where a source gives them. Not covered: monument loot (see rust-monuments-loot), weapon damage (rust-combat-damage-model), farming and cooking (rust-farming-food), turrets (rust-turrets-deployables). Vanilla PC servers only.
title: Rust Wildlife and NPCs

text:
- **Livestock:** domesticated cows and sheep that can be bred and sold [1].
- **Critter:** decorative wildlife such as frogs and rabbits, heavily budgeted [1].
- **Scientist:** a hostile armed NPC found at monuments and roadsides [4].
- **Bradley APC:** a tracked armoured vehicle NPC patrolling Launch Site [5].
- **Patrol Helicopter:** a roaming helicopter event [5].
title: Rust Wildlife and NPCs

text:
**Livestock.** Cows and sheep both produce dung; cows produce milk and sheep wool; both yield meat, bones and leather when harvested [1]. They have genetics and needs and can be bred, though Facepunch says genes do not behave exactly like plant genes [1]. Grown animals can be sold to a Stable vendor; offers vary with gene quality, you can reject an offer twice more, after which the vendor refuses that animal for 15 minutes [1]. Wool is traded in with three offers, to a maximum of 400 wool per trade-in [1]. Milk refrigerated for 4 hours can be skimmed into Skimmed Milk and Cream [1]. New animal gate and fence deployables contain livestock [1].

**Critters.** Frogs, rabbits, squirrels, sea turtles, crabs and jellyfish appear in suitable biomes and are mostly set dressing under a tight budget [1].

**Wild animals.** A community bestiary describes bears, boars, wolves and stags as melee animals, chickens as passive, and sharks as ocean attackers that strike, retreat and circle [4]. Since the June 2021 AI overhaul all AI runs under one system, with wolves gathering in groups of up to 3 and deer in packs of up to 5 [6]. Pigs yield Raw Pork, 8 Flesh per pig on the wiki [3].

**Scientists and guards.** The bestiary lists scientists by location: Oil Rig heavy scientists with M249, Minigun, Spas-12 or Flamethrower, Outpost peacekeepers, and roadside and junkpile scientists with an M92 [4]. Keycard drops are covered in rust-monuments-loot.

**Navigation and performance.** NPCs use a new navmesh that lets them enter structures and respect doors [1]. Only a subset is processed per frame under a hardcoded time cap, and navigation performance was at least doubled since the previous patch [1].

**Bradley APC.** It patrols the paved roads of Launch Site, its only spawn, and is described as damaged only by explosives; it fires a machine gun and cannon at detected players and repairs itself if left alone for minutes [5]. Its kill drops 3 APC crates [5] (the 2017 launch post said 1 or 2 [8], now outdated), and the wiki defines the Bradley Crate as a 7-slot container [2].

**Patrol Helicopter.** A roaming event roughly every 2 to 4 hours depending on server configuration; it attacks with machine-gun strafing and rockets, and downing both rotors destroys it [5]. A second guide (updated 25 Aug 2024) gives the same 10,000 body health and 900 and 500 rotor health, and describes the crate loot as strong raiding and building tools without a count [7]. Its crash site holds about 3 to 4 locked crates [5].

## Guidance 1 — Bring explosives, not bullets, for Bradley

- **Guidance:** Plan Bradley attempts around explosive ammunition and spare rockets.

- **Evidence basis:** Facepunch documents fences and the 15 minute refusal after rejected offers [1].
- **Confidence:** Medium. Facts are primary, tactics are judgement.
- **So what:** Avoids losing a bred animal's sale window.

text:
This deep-dive covers Rust's server-driven world events: the Cargo Ship, airdrops and the Supply Signal, the Chinook locked-crate event, the Patrol Helicopter, the Bradley APC and the Satellite Crash event added in 2026. It goes deeper than rust-game-mechanics-foundation and leaves NPC statistics to rust-wildlife-npcs.

Mechanics and loot tables come from Facepunch devblogs and the Facepunch wiki, so they are primary. But most spawn timings are stated only in devblogs from 2015 to 2018 and no current-build value was found for them. The Livestock Update of 1 October 2026 contains one cargo ship fix and no airdrop, Bradley, helicopter or Chinook change [1]. The document is rated Medium: mechanics are well sourced, current timers are not.
title: Rust World Events
topic: Cargo ship, airdrops and map events

text:
- The Cargo Ship fills with loot on spawn, refreshes it every 10 minutes for up to three rounds, and departs after 50 minutes by default; the refresh timing and duration were configurable per the 2018 devblog [6].
- Since April 2024 the ship docks at a harbour, and from May 2024 at both harbours if they exist, before leaving [7][8].
- The Livestock Update (1 October 2026) lists one cargo ship fix and no airdrop, helicopter, Bradley or Chinook change [1].
- The Airdrop container has 14 slots and a 40-entry loot table on the wiki, checked against the Livestock build [13].
- The Chinook event delivers a locked crate that needs a timed hack; damage to the computer slows it [9].
- Power Trip (6 August 2026) added a Satellite Crash event and Airfield terminals that raise airdrop rate and call a Chinook resupply [3].
- Breach and Clear (3 September 2026) improved save/load of Patrol Helicopter, Bradley, cargo and satellite events [2].
- No current-build Facepunch figure was found for how often the Patrol Helicopter or an airdrop spawns (see Open Questions).
title: Rust World Events
topic: Cargo ship, airdrops and map events

text: Covered: Cargo Ship, airdrops, Supply Signal, Chinook locked crate, Patrol Helicopter, Bradley APC and the Satellite Crash event, on vanilla PC servers, checked against the Livestock Update (1 October 2026). Not covered: NPC health and weapons (see rust-wildlife-npcs), fixed-monument loot (rust-monuments-loot), vehicles (rust-vehicles), seasonal cosmetic events, and Twitch Drops promotions, which are not in-game world events [1]. Oil Rig is mentioned only where a 2026 fix touches it.

text:
- **Server event:** a periodic, server-spawned occurrence rather than a fixed monument; Facepunch applies this term to the Cargo Ship, Patrol Helicopter and Chinook [5][9][10].
- **Locked crate:** a crate that must be hacked with a timer before opening [9].
- **Supply Signal:** a purple smoke grenade used to mark a spot for an airdrop [14].
- **Loot round:** a Cargo Ship refill of its crates [6].
title: Rust World Events
topic: Cargo ship, airdrops and map events

text:
**Evidence layer.** Dates reflect when Facepunch described the behaviour; only the Livestock Update statement is tied to the checked build.

**Cargo Ship.** Introduced in 2018 as the CCSC Lazarus, a periodic server event that "will trigger every two to four in-game days" and patrols about 200 metres offshore [5]. Players board by boat and mount a ladder; two codelocked crates are hacked after clearing the defending Scientists, turret-style Scientists never move, and the whole server can see the ship on the map [5]. A radiation alarm warns that the cargo is unstable and it is time to leave [5]. A later 2018 devblog changed it to loot rounds: on spawn, 1 Locked Crate, 1 Elite Crate, 4 Military Crates and 4 Regular Crates appear, including below deck; loot respawns every 10 minutes for three rounds, a horn signals each new round, and the ship departs after 50 minutes [6]. In April 2024 harbour docking arrived: the ship picks the first harbour it passes and docks once, cranes load containers onto the deck, and docking attempts one loot refresh, with no further loot once all three rounds are used [7]. In May 2024 it was changed to dock at both harbours if they exist, containers spawn when the approach starts, and the map shows whether it has docked [8]. Event save/load was improved in September 2026 [2].

**Airdrops.** The wiki describes the Supply Signal as purple smoke marking a location for an airdrop [14]. Airdrop loot was made to guarantee more good items and less junk in the April 2018 vehicle update [9], and in 2017 was set to always drop two weapons plus ammo and two armour pieces [12]. Power Trip adds a smaller Airfield terminal which, when charged, raises the rate at which airdrops fall across the map; it slowly loses charge [3]. The wiki does not state an airdrop interval [13].

**Chinook locked crate.** A periodic server event that appears offshore and flies to a drop zone at most Tier 1 and above monuments, orbits to neutralise threats, then releases a locked crate [9]. Pressing use starts the timer; damaging the computer slows it, and all maps show an icon for locked supply crates [9]. Power Trip also lets a charged larger Airfield terminal call a Chinook resupply crate near the airfield tarmac [3].

**Patrol Helicopter.** Devblog 78 (2015) said one spawns offshore every 48 to 72 in-game hours and patrols between monuments [10]. Waves of Change (April 2024) randomises attack-run values, adds an orbit phase, scores invisible zones by damage taken and makes it flee no-go zones [7]. Meta Madness (May 2024) makes it try to crash at a nearby non-safe-zone monument on death, flee when a player quickly removes 30% of its HP, and target players on boats, cargo and trains [8]. Its crash drops a Helicopter Crate [16].

**Bradley APC.** Added to Launch Site in August 2017, with a main cannon and coaxial machine gun and slim initial loot [11], and to Materials Extraction (Hapis) in November 2017 [12]. Waves of Change lets Scientists deploy from it, at Launch Site and on roads at the end of the month [7]. Meta Madness spawns them in stages: 2 at 80% health, 4 more at 60%, 6 more at 40% [8]. The admin command bradley.quickrespawn respawns the Launch Site Bradley [18].

**Satellite Crash.** Added in Power Trip: a Satellite Control Computer at Launch Site is powered and aimed, the satellite descends visibly to all players, and spills crates that must cool before looting [3]. The post gives no counts or timers [3].

text:
## Guidance 1 — Treat all event timers as server-specific and verify them

- **Guidance:** Do not plan around a fixed spawn interval; check the server's own settings or observe a cycle.
- **Evidence basis:** Interval values date from 2015 and 2018 devblogs [5][10], and a community guide says heli frequency depends on configuration [19].
- **Confidence:** Medium. The age of the sources is documented; the practical advice is judgement.
- **So what:** Admins should state event settings in the server description; players should not rely on a wiki number.

## Guidance 2 — Loot the Cargo Ship early and know your rounds

- **Guidance:** Arrive before the first horn and plan for the docking refresh rather than waiting for a late round.
- **Evidence basis:** Three rounds, 10-minute spacing, a docking refresh and an end-of-loot rule are described in devblogs [6][7].
- **Confidence:** Medium. The mechanics are primary but their defaults may have changed.
- **So what:** Fewer wasted trips and less exposure to the contested harbour.

## Guidance 3 — Expect Bradley to bring reinforcements

- **Guidance:** Plan ammunition and cover for 12 extra Scientists across the fight, not just the APC.
- **Evidence basis:** Stage spawns at 80, 60 and 40% health [8], and the Bradley Crate lists rockets as guaranteed [15].
- **Confidence:** Medium. Stage thresholds are from May 2024 and not rechecked in 2026.
- **So what:** Solo attempts are costlier than the crate alone suggests.

title: Rust Clothing and Armour

text:
This deep-dive extends rust-items-crafting-foundation with the wearable side of the game: the slot and layer model, per-item protection percentages, the cold penalty carried by metal gear, radiation protection, and the workbench, ingredient and research costs listed on Facepunch wiki item pages. Values were read on 2026-10-08, when the Livestock Update (1 October 2026) was the latest update [1]. Combat results are covered in rust-combat-damage-model and are not repeated here.

Document confidence is Medium. Every per-item number comes from a Facepunch wiki item page, but those pages are undated, do not state body areas, and do not say how stacked items combine numerically; the wiki only says both stacked items contribute their stats [2]. Warmth is not a separate stat on the pages opened, only a Cold protection percentage.
title: Rust Clothing and Armour

text:
- Head, Chest and Legs each have two layers (Layer 1 clothing, Layer 2 armour); Hands and Feet take one item each; full-body suits replace every slot [2].
- Some items occupy both layers of a slot, so nothing else fits there: Metal Facemask, Coffee Can Helmet, Heavy Plate Jacket, Heavy Plate Pants [2].
- The Heavy Plate set lists 75 to 90% projectile and 70 to 80% melee protection with 100% explosion, but Cold of -67% (jacket), -17% (pants) and -16% (helmet) [5][6][7].
- The Hazmat Suit lists Radiation 50% and Cold 50% with 30% projectile, melee and explosion, and needs Workbench Level 2 [8].
- Wood armour and the Hide Vest are known by default and need no workbench [16][17][18].
- No clothing or armour value change is listed in the Livestock Update changelog [1].
- Armour and cold protection trade off: metal pieces carry negative Cold values *(assessed from the tables below)*.

Not covered: how damage is calculated in combat (see rust-combat-damage-model), weapons (rust-weapons-ammo), skins (rust-skins-cosmetics), and items not opened for this document, including the Snow Jacket, Bone Armor, Arctic Suit, Wetsuit, gloves and boots, whose stats were not read. title: Rust Clothing and Armour

text:
- **Layer 1 / Layer 2:** the clothing layer worn underneath and the armour layer on top, for Head, Chest and Legs [2].
- **Dual-layer item:** an item occupying both layers of one slot [2].
- **Protection:** a percentage per damage type listed on an item page, such as Projectile, Melee, Bite, Radiation, Cold and Explosion [3][5].
- **Negative protection:** a listed value below zero, for example Cold -34% [4].
title: Rust Clothing and Armour

text:
**Evidence layer.**

**Slots and layers.** The Facepunch wiki states that Head, Chest and Legs each have two layers. Head Layer 1 holds hats and bandanas, Layer 2 helmets and face masks; Chest Layer 1 holds shirts and hoodies, Layer 2 jackets and plate carriers; Legs Layer 1 holds pants and shorts, Layer 2 kilts and plate legs. Hands and Feet hold one item each [2].

**Stacking.** One item per layer may be worn, so two items per slot, for example a Hoodie with a Road Sign Jacket or Pants with a Road Sign Kilt. The wiki says both stacked items contribute their stats and that Layer 1 provides comfort and cold resistance while Layer 2 provides projectile and melee protection, but it gives no numbers for how contributions combine [2]. A community guide dated 11 June 2026 repeats that "both layers contribute their stats" [19]. Item pages are not fully consistent with that generalisation: the Hoodie (Layer 1) lists Projectile 20% and Melee 15% [9], and the Jacket is listed on the Armor layer with Cold 40% [10].

**Dual-layer and multi-slot items.** The wiki lists the Metal Facemask and Coffee Can Helmet (Head), Heavy Plate Jacket and Snow Jacket (Chest) and Heavy Plate Pants (Legs) as occupying both layers. Bone Armor covers Chest and Legs plus Hands and Feet; the Wetsuit takes Chest and Legs Layer 1 only; the Chicken Costume takes Chest and Legs Layer 2 only [2]. The Hazmat Suit and Arctic Suit are full-body and exclude all other clothing [2]. The Hazmat Suit page lists slot and layer as Full Body [8].

**Protection is per damage type, not warmth.** Item pages list Cold as a protection percentage; no separate warmth value was found on any page opened [3][4][8][9]. Metal and plate items list negative Cold, while cloth items list positive Cold [4][5][9][11].

**Radiation.** Most items list small Radiation protection (3 to 7%); the Hazmat Suit lists 50% [8][9][14][15][18]. The radiation levels of monuments are outside this document; see rust-monuments-loot and rust-game-mechanics-foundation.

**Crafting, research and repair.** Each page lists a recipe, a required workbench with craft times per level, Research Table cost and Workbench Tech Tree cost, and a Repair Bench cost with 20% condition loss for repairable items [3][4][5][8]. The Hoodie and Wood Chestplate pages list Repairable as False [9][16]. Wood armour and Hide Vest pages state that the blueprint is known by default [16][17][18].

text:
## Guidance 1 — Pair every metal or plate piece with warm Layer 1 clothing in cold areas

- **Guidance:** Treat Cold as a cost of armour and choose Layer 1 items to offset it.
- **Evidence basis:** Metal Chest Plate -34, Road Sign Jacket -34, Heavy Plate Jacket -67 versus Hoodie +34 [4][12][5][9]; layers both contribute [2].
- **Confidence:** Medium. Values are primary; the net temperature result is not sourced.
- **So what:** Check your cold status in game after changing gear.

## Guidance 2 — Choose Hazmat for radiation and Heavy Plate for fights, not one for both

- **Guidance:** Use the Hazmat Suit when radiation is the threat and Heavy Plate when player damage is.
- **Evidence basis:** Hazmat Radiation 50%, Projectile 30% [8]; Heavy Plate Radiation 7%, Projectile 75 to 90% [5][6][7].
- **Confidence:** Medium. It rests on listed percentages; radiation intensity is not covered.
- **So what:** Hazmat occupies every slot, so you cannot add armour on top [2].

## Guidance 3 — Early armour is cheap and workbench-free but narrow

- **Guidance:** Wood armour suits early melee fights; do not expect it to stop bullets.
- **Evidence basis:** Wood Chestplate Melee 40%, Projectile 10%, known by default [16][17].
- **Confidence:** Medium. Values primary; fight outcomes are inference.
- **So what:** Upgrade toward Road Sign or Heavy Plate once a workbench is available [5][12].

title: Rust Economy and Trading

text:
Rust has no formal currency. Scrap is described by the wiki as "often used as a currency", and it is also the research and workbench input [9]. Trade happens through four systems: player-run vending machines, NPC vendors that pay or charge scrap at safe-zone monuments, a drone marketplace that delivers from vending machines for a scrap fee, and, since July 2026, rentable shops at the Apartment Complex [3][5][12]. Recyclers convert items back into raw materials and so set the floor price of components [10][11].

The design intent and mechanics come from Facepunch devblogs, but most numbers (recycler efficiency, scrap drop tables, vending cost) come from undated wiki pages, and NPC buy and sell price tables could not be sourced at all. Confidence is Medium: Facepunch sources cover the systems, while current values rest on wiki pages that one Facepunch post already contradicts [2][10].
title: Rust Economy and Trading

text:
- Scrap stacks to 1,000, despawns after 20 minutes on the ground, and cannot be crafted, repaired, recycled or researched [9].
- The drone marketplace at Bandit Camp and Outpost charges a 20 scrap delivery fee per trade (Softcore update, 4 February 2021); delivery can take up to five minutes [5].
- Items sold to NPC vending machines for scrap use dynamic pricing: each item starts the wipe at 50% less value and can rise by an extra 100% if none are sold (5 December 2024) [4].
- Rentable shops (Common Ground, 2 July 2026) need at least 12 hours of rent to open, can be taken over after 6 hours at 2x cost, and drones cannot reach them [3].
- A Vending Machine crafts from 20 High Quality Metal and 3 Gears at Workbench Level 1 per the wiki [8], matching the cost cut in Devblog 180 [7].
- Green recycler efficiency fell to a 50% baseline in Power Trip (6 August 2026); the wiki Recycler page still says 60%, so it is stale on that point [2][10].
- The Safe Zone Recycler is listed at 40% yield and 8 seconds per item [11].
- The Livestock Update (1 October 2026) added a Stable vendor that buys animals and wool and a "vendor bartering mechanic" that the post does not explain [1].

title: Rust Economy and Trading

text:
- **Scrap** — dropped currency-like item used for research, workbench use, and trading [9].
- **Vending machine** — a player-deployed shop where the owner sets sell orders and buyers pay from their inventory [8][13].
- **NPC vendor** — an NPC vending machine at a safe-zone monument that trades goods for scrap [4][12].
- **Marketplace** — drone-delivery terminals at Bandit Camp and Outpost [5].
- **Rentable shop** — a rented stall at the Apartment Complex [3].
- **Recycler** — a station that breaks items into component materials at a stated efficiency [2][10].
- **Safe zone** — a monument area covered by turrets where hostile acts are punished; see rust-monuments-loot [12].
title: Rust Economy and Trading

text:
**Evidence layer.**

**Scrap as currency and input.** The wiki describes scrap as used at Research Tables and Workbenches and "often used as a currency" [9]. It is not craftable and comes from loot: barrels give 2, Basic Crates 3, Military Crates 8, Elite Crates 25, Airdrops 140-160 at 55.6%, and scientists 8-24 at 36.3% [9]. It is also an ingredient for items including Gears (100) and Research Table (20) [9]. Helicopter shredding at the Junkyard pays scrap by type and health: 200 for a Minicopter, 300 for a Scrap Transport Helicopter and 500 for an Attack Helicopter (Polish and Progress, 5 December 2024) [4].

**Player vending machines.** Each machine has a front for buyers and a back for the owner, who stocks items and sets sell orders; payments land in the machine's storage [13]. That description dates from the February 2017 introduction, when the cap was 7 orders and the craft cost 50 HQM [13]; Devblog 180 later cut the cost to 20 HQM and 3 Gears and made it a default blueprint [7]. The wiki page confirms the current 20 HQM and 3 Gears cost and a 5 rW power input [8]. The May 2026 update redesigned the admin page, allowing orders to be set up from the built-in inventory, skins sold individually, and existing orders reordered [6]. Raiders who reach the rear panel can take the contents [8].

**Vending statistics.** Since 5 December 2024 owners can see transaction history, highest-revenue items, best sellers and customer stats; convars `vendingmachine.max_returned`, `vendingmachine.max_processed` and `vendingmachine.max_history` limit the queries and stored history, and machines show whether they are drone accessible [4].

**NPC vendors and dynamic pricing.** Safe-zone monuments such as the Outpost have vending machines selling resources and valuable items [12]. Scrap paid by NPC vending machines for items is dynamic: items start each wipe at 50% less value and can rise by up to an extra 100% when unsold [4]. Power Trip cut water-well vendor stock from 10 to 2 and lengthened restock from 2 to 10 minutes, leaving prices unchanged [2]. Livestock added a Stable vendor that buys grown cattle and sheep at a random offer based on gene quality (up to two re-rolls, then a 15 minute lockout) and buys wool, with the offer depending on the amount brought, up to 400 [1].

**Drone marketplace.** Introduced 4 February 2021 at Bandit Camp and Outpost, it lets a player choose a vending machine at a terminal and order from it for a 20 scrap fee, with delivery taking up to five minutes [5]. Orders can target any public vending machine and all NPC shops, but not machines outside open areas, and drones cannot be destroyed [5]. Terminals are locked to the buyer for 10 minutes [5]. The Livestock post states the marketplace needs power and that outages on low-population servers had blocked trade, so Heavy Fuses now last longer on servers of 10 or fewer players [1].

**Rentable shops.** At the Apartment Complex, a shop contract shows a non-refundable upfront scrap fee plus an hourly scrap rent, and at least 12 hours of rent is needed to open [3]. A shop can be taken over after 6 hours open at 2x cost (3x, 4x on later takeovers); the multiplier resets when rent runs out [3]. Shops are managed like vending machines but drones cannot access them [3]. The former owner has 24 hours to retrieve items, and the master key opens shops [3].

**Recyclers.** The wiki Recycler page lists 60% yield and 5 seconds per item [10]. Power Trip states the green recycler baseline is now 50%, rising to 60% with enough power-plant power, with duration falling from 5 s to 4.5 s at maximum power; a red recycler at the Power Plant gives 75% at maximum power only; yellow (safe-zone) recyclers are unchanged [2]. The Safe Zone Recycler page lists 40% and 8 seconds, at Outpost and Bandit Camp [11]. The vending machine item page lists recycling outputs of 12 HQM for the standard recycler and 8 HQM for the safe-zone one [8].

text:
**Judgement layer.**

## Guidance 1 — Recheck recycler numbers in game before planning scrap income

- **Guidance:** Do not use the wiki's 60% green recycler figure; verify efficiency in game and assume it varies with Power Plant output.
- **Evidence basis:** Power Trip changed the baseline to 50% while the wiki page is undated and still lists 60% [2][10].
- **Confidence:** Medium. The contradiction is documented, but which value is live was not tested in game.
- **So what:** Recycling plans and yield tables copied from older guides will overstate returns.

## Guidance 2 — Treat NPC scrap sales as a spread-out income, not a repeat one

- **Guidance:** Sell varied items across the wipe rather than dumping one type repeatedly.
- **Evidence basis:** Dynamic pricing starts at -50% and rises up to +100% only when an item is unsold [4].
- **Confidence:** Medium. The mechanism is primary, but the exact curve is not published in the sources opened.
- **So what:** Players who sell the same item repeatedly earn less per unit.

## Guidance 3 — Use the marketplace for safety, but collect immediately

- **Guidance:** Order via drone when travel is risky, and stay at the terminal to collect.
- **Evidence basis:** Drones cannot be destroyed and the terminal locks to you for 10 minutes [5].
- **Confidence:** Medium. Facepunch states the design aim, but the post is from 2021 and later behaviour was only partly rechecked.
- **So what:** A 20 scrap fee buys a protected transfer, with a time limit to claim it.

## Guidance 4 — Price rentable shops against rent plus takeover risk

- **Guidance:** Only open a shop if sales will cover the upfront fee and at least 12 hours of rent, and keep valuables out.
- **Evidence basis:** Fee, rent, 6 hour takeover and master key access are stated [3].
- **Confidence:** Low. The scrap amounts are not published in sources opened, so profitability is unquantified.
- **So what:** Treat shops as a small-scale convenience until costs are confirmed in game.

title: Rust Farming and Food

text:
This deep-dive covers how Rust food is produced and prepared: planters and plant genetics, the Cooking Workbench and its food and tea recipes, selected food stats, and the livestock products added by the Livestock Update of 1 October 2026. It goes deeper than rust-items-crafting-foundation, which only lists Food as a wiki category.

The Facepunch devblog confirms the livestock design (cows, sheep, genetics, milk, wool, the stable vendor, fencing) but gives almost no numbers [1]. Most numbers come from Rust Wiki pages that have no build date [2][3][4]. Confidence is Medium: the structure is primary-sourced, but values are undated and many gaps (growth times, crop yields, livestock gene mechanics) could not be sourced.
title: Rust Farming and Food

text:
- Each plant has six gene slots; the genes are G (growth), Y (yield), H (hardiness), W (water intake) and X (empty). W and X are the only bad genes [2].
- A Small Planter Box costs 100 Wood and 1 Tarp and holds 3 seeds [5].
- The Cooking Workbench requires Workbench Level 2 and costs 200 Metal Fragments, 200 Stones and 100 Wood [4].
- Pies and teas are mixed at the Cooking Workbench; pies take 30 s, bread 20 s, teas 5 s [4].
- The Livestock Update (1 October 2026) added cows and sheep with genetics, milk, wool, meat, bones, leather and a stable vendor [1].
- Milk refrigerated for 4 hours can be skimmed into Skimmed Milk and Cream; milk lengthens tea effects and cream increases their potency [1].
- Wool sales to the stable vendor are capped at 400 wool per trade and the vendor gives three offers [1].

title: Rust Farming and Food

text:
- **Gene** — one of six slots on a plant, letters G, Y, H, W, X [2].
- **Clone** — a copy of a plant that carries its genes, obtained from grown plants [3].
- **Planter** — a deployable that holds seeds, for example the Small Planter Box [5].
- **Cooking Workbench** — a deployable that mixes advanced food, tea, fuel and ammunition recipes [4].
- **Stable vendor** — NPC at a Stable who buys grown animals and wool [1].
title: Rust Farming and Food

text:
**Evidence layer.**

**Planting and genes.** Seeds drop from picking wild plants, for example corn, and can be planted in the ground or in a planter [7]. Planting in a planter with large quantities of water gives more produce and faster growth, though the wiki does not quantify this [7]. Each plant has six gene slots, assigned randomly when the seed is planted [2]. Planting several plants adjacent lets one plant's genes override others through crossbreeding [2].

**Genes.** G raises growth rate, Y raises yield, H raises resistance to bad temperatures and biomes, W raises water consumption and can make a plant unhealthy if it dominates, and X is an empty slot [2][3]. The wiki states the combinations GGGYYY and GGYYYY: the first gives higher production and 3 clones when cloned, the second slightly lower production and 4 clones [3].

**Water supply.** The wiki's Farming Basics describes sprinkler farms. Freshwater is supplied by a powered water pump to up to 4 sprinklers; salt water needs 2 pumps into a powered water purifier; a modular car water tanker can feed water barrels, each supporting up to 6 sprinklers [3]. A 3-planter layout fills at 5 mL and a 6-planter layout at 4 mL; in the 3-planter layout sprinklers must not see more than three planters [3].

**Fertiliser.** The Composter produces fertiliser from compostable items [8].

**Cooking.** The Cooking Workbench cooks raw meats into cooked versions in 3.8 s (fish 2.5 s, horse 3.2 s) and mixes pies, bread and teas [4]. Teas come in tiers: four basic teas make one Advanced tea, and four Advanced make one Pure tea of the same type [4].

**Livestock.** Cows and sheep both produce dung; cows also give milk and sheep wool; animals can be harvested for meat, bones and leather [1]. Animals have genetics and needs and can be bred, but the devblog says genes "won't behave exactly like plants", so plant breeding techniques may not transfer [1]. Grown animals can be sold at a Stable for resources based on gene quality, with up to three offers; after rejecting the third, the vendor refuses that animal for 15 minutes [1]. Animal gates and fences contain livestock, and with the new navmesh NPCs can enter player structures [1]. The Biofuel Generator turns organic matter, including raw or spoiled meat, into Low Grade Fuel and needs stirring again after about 30 minutes [1].

**Milk chain.** Milk can be drunk as is; after 4 hours refrigerated it can be skimmed into Skimmed Milk and Cream [1]. New Creamy and Milky variants of most pure teas were added [1].

text:
This document is the entry point for how Rust turns raw resources into items. It covers gathered resources, crafting, the three workbench tiers, the blueprint and research system, scrap, and the wiki's item categories. It is an overview. Weapon, ammunition and component deep-dives are separate documents.

The core loop is documented by Facepunch: items are locked unless a blueprint is known, workbenches gate tiers, and scrap pays for research [3]. Workbench levels 2 and 3 need blueprint fragments [2], and since the Pivot or Die update of 6 November 2025 workbench crafting costs no scrap, the tech tree tax is gone and all blueprints were wiped once [16]. Scrap-cost detail is in rust-research-blueprints. Confidence is Medium: the system design rests on Facepunch devblogs, but exact costs come from Rust Wiki item pages that carry no build date, and the October 2026 update was checked only for relevance [1].
title: Rust Items and Crafting: Foundation

text:
- Items are locked except default blueprints; a research bench turns a found item plus scrap into a blueprint with no chance of failure (devblog of 2017) [3].
- Workbenches come in three tiers, must be built in order, and let you craft anything at or below their tier; a higher bench than the item requires crafts faster [3].
- Workbench Level 1 costs 500 Wood and 100 Metal Fragments per the wiki [5].
- Since 2 October 2025, Workbench Level 2 requires 5 Basic Blueprint Fragments and Level 3 requires 5 Advanced Blueprint Fragments [2].
- 20 Basic Blueprint Fragments convert into 1 Advanced Blueprint Fragment [2].
- Pivot or Die (6 November 2025) removed scrap crafting costs from workbenches, removed the tech tree tax, greatly reduced scrap research costs and wiped all blueprints; Blueprint Fragment requirements were unchanged [16]. See rust-research-blueprints.
- The wiki lists Research Table research at 60 Scrap and states the blueprint is known by default; research is only needed for a physical blueprint for the Industrial Crafter [8].
- The Livestock Update of 1 October 2026 added milk, wool and food recipes but does not mention scrap, research or workbench systems [1].

text:
- **Blueprint** — an item that teaches a specific recipe [10].
- **Scrap** — a currency-like resource used at the research table and workbench [9].
- **Workbench tier** — Level 1, 2 or 3, gating which recipes are craftable [3].
- **Blueprint fragments** — Basic and Advanced fragments, ingredients for Workbench Levels 2 and 3 [11][12].
- **Research table** — a deployable that converts an item plus scrap into a blueprint [8][10].
title: Rust Items and Crafting: Foundation

text:
**Evidence layer.**

**Locked items and blueprints.** Since Devblog 180 (5 October 2017) all items except default blueprints are locked. Players start with default blueprints such as campfires, furnaces, workbenches and storage [3]. Repairing an item also requires its blueprint [3].

**Research.** A looted item is taken to a research bench and scrap is paid to create a blueprint; the devblog states there is no percentage chance of failure [3]. The wiki states the scrap cost depends on the item's rarity or quality, that blueprints also drop in crates and barrels, and that the table does not check whether you already know the recipe, so scrap can be wasted [10]. Once researched, a blueprint can be studied to permanently learn the recipe [3].

**Workbench experimentation.** Devblog 185 (9 November 2017) added an Experiment UI where scrap produces a random blueprint for that tier that avoids ones already learned [4]. The wiki also notes each workbench has a tech tree for targeting a specific item instead of relying on random drops [10]. Pivot or Die removed the "tech tree tax" and cut research scrap costs by rarity [16]; see rust-research-blueprints for the figures. The experiment UI was not re-verified against the current build.

**Workbench tiers.** There are three tiers, each requiring the previous tier to craft [3]. Standing near an active workbench lets you craft anything at that tier and below, and crafting is much faster when the bench tier exceeds the item's requirement [3]. Wiki craft times show this: the Research Table takes 30 s at Level 1, 15 s at Level 2, and 7 s at Level 3 [8].

**Fragment gate.** From the Meta Shift update (2 October 2025), Level 2 and 3 workbenches need 5 Basic and 5 Advanced Blueprint Fragments respectively, a stated soft gate pushing players to monuments [2]. The same update says scrap crafting costs for levels 2 and 3 were greatly reduced [2]. Pivot or Die (6 November 2025) then removed scrap crafting costs from workbenches entirely while leaving fragment requirements unchanged [16]; the wiki recipes for Levels 2 and 3 list no scrap [6][7]. Its changelog speaks of "Workbenches" generally and does not name Levels 2 and 3 [16].

**Blueprint wipe.** Pivot or Die wiped all blueprints and all servers on 6 November 2025 [16]; see rust-research-blueprints for wipe behaviour.

**Resources.** Wood is collected from trees and is an ingredient in many recipes [13]. Metal ore and sulfur ore are smelted in furnaces into metal fragments and sulfur [14][15]. Scrap is not craftable and is obtained from loot such as crates, barrels, airdrops and scientists [9]. The October 2026 update added livestock products (milk, wool, meat, bones, leather) as new harvestable resources [1].

**Item categories.** The Rust Wiki groups items into Weapons, Construction, Items, Resources, Attire, Tools, Medical, Food, Ammo, Traps, Components, Electrical, Fun and Misc [17].

text:
**Evidence layer.**

**Two routes to learn an item.** Since Devblog 180 (5 October 2017), items are locked except default blueprints. A found item taken to a research bench becomes a blueprint with no chance of failure, and the blueprint can be studied to learn the recipe permanently or traded [4]. Devblog 185 (9 November 2017) added a workbench Experiment UI that spends scrap on a random blueprint for that tier, avoiding ones already learned [5]. The wiki says each workbench has a tech tree for targeting a specific item [9].

**Cost depends on rarity.** The wiki states the research cost varies by item rarity or quality, and each tech tree item has its own cost [9]. Facepunch gave the four rarity-tier scrap values in the Pivot or Die changelog [3] (table below).

**The table does not check.** The research table does not stop you researching an item you already know, so scrap can be wasted [9].

**Workbench crafting and scrap.** Devblog 180 said building workbenches takes significant scrap, without figures [4]. Pivot or Die removed scrap crafting costs from workbenches; scrap now goes to unlocks [3]. Wiki recipes for Levels 2 and 3 list metal fragments, High Quality Metal and blueprint fragments, not scrap [6][7].

**Learning workbench blueprints.** Workbench 2 and 3 are known by default; research is needed only to obtain a physical blueprint for the Industrial Crafter, at 30 Scrap each [6][7].

**Blueprint loss.** Facepunch sources reviewed describe no loss on death; Devblog 180 does not mention a death penalty [4]. Loss occurs through wipes: Pivot or Die wiped all blueprints and servers [3]. Rustafied reports monthly forced blueprint wipes on official servers, citing a social post, and the same article calls it an undated edit [18]. The Facepunch devblog itself does not commit to monthly wipes [3].

**Scrap supply.** Scrap is not craftable; it comes from loot, for example Elite Crate 25 and Military Crate 8, Locked Crate 140-160 at 33.3% [10].

text:
This document goes deeper than rust-items-crafting-foundation on the tools players use to collect resources: the rock, the stone and metal hatchets and pickaxes, the salvaged axe and icepick, the chainsaw and the jackhammer. It records what each tool costs, which targets it can harvest, the wiki's gather figures, how ore nodes and the hotspot minigame work, and what the recycler returns when a tool is broken down.

The headline limit is that no Facepunch page opened states the resource yield per hit. The wiki lists a "Gather Damage" and a "Bonus" figure per target but does not explain them, so this document reports them as published and does not convert them into resources per swing. The foundation's gather-rate gap therefore stays open. Confidence is Medium: item data and recycler efficiency come from first-party sources, but the wiki pages are undated and the gather columns are undefined.
title: Rust Tools and Gathering

text:
- Ore nodes come in three types, stone, sulfur and metal, and are found around cliffs and rock formations [4].
- The hotspot minigame (Devblog 170, 27 July 2017) raises a hit to 150% and consecutive hits to 300%, but Facepunch states it does not increase the total resources in a node [3][4].
- Wiki "Gather Damage" per target: Rock 5 (ore) and 10 (tree); Stone Pickaxe 16 (ore); Pickaxe 30 (ore); Salvaged Icepick 50 (ore); Jackhammer 25 (ore); Stone Hatchet 20 (tree); Hatchet 30 (tree); Salvaged Axe 50 (tree); Chainsaw 30 (tree) [5][6][7][8][9][10][11][12][13].
- The Jackhammer is not craftable and not researchable; the wiki lists airdrops and locked crates as loot sources [13].
- Since Power Trip (6 August 2026), green recyclers run at 50% efficiency, restoring to 60% with sufficient Power Plant power, and a single red recycler at the Power Plant runs at 75% only at maximum power [2].
- Ore nodes and woodpiles can no longer spawn in safe zones, because they could only be harvested with a rock and piled up, draining the global spawn population [2].
- Vanilla Rust has no built-in gather-rate multiplier convar according to one hosting guide; multipliers need a plugin such as GatherManager *(community source)* [20].
title: Rust Tools and Gathering

text: Covers vanilla PC Rust: hand tools for gathering, the three ore node types, the hotspot minigame, the ore and wood items nodes give, the recycler's effect on tools, and the admin-only quarry's status. Excludes console, modded recipes, weapon use of these tools in combat (see rust-combat-damage-model), animal harvesting detail (see rust-wildlife-npcs), and server gather-rate plugins beyond a note. Checked against the Livestock Update of 1 October 2026 [1].
title: Rust Tools and Gathering

text:
- **Ore node** — a stone, sulfur or metal rock formation harvested with a pickaxe-class tool [4].
- **Hotspot** — a shimmering weak point on an ore node that boosts yield per hit [3][4].
- **Gather Damage / Bonus / Condition Loss** — the three columns the Rust Wiki prints per target; the wiki does not define the first two [5][8].
- **Recycler** — a station that converts items into components at a percentage of their value [14][15].
- **Safe Zone Recycler** — the protected recycler at Outpost and Bandit Camp, also called the yellow recycler [2][15].
title: Rust Tools and Gathering

text:
**Evidence layer.**

**Nodes.** The wiki names three ore node types: stone, sulfur and metal, mostly around cliffs, mountains and rock formations [4]. Harvesting yields ore items: Stones (stack 1000), Metal Ore (stack 1000) and Sulfur Ore (stack 1000), which the wiki lists as gathered from node sources [16][17][18]. Metal ore and sulfur ore are smelted in furnaces into Metal Fragments and Sulfur [16][18].

**Hotspot minigame.** Devblog 170 introduced a shimmering hotspot on nearby ore. Hitting one boosts gathering to 150%, each successive hit raises it, up to 300%, and a miss resets the bonus [3]. Facepunch states you do not earn more resources overall, but you harvest the node faster [3]. The devblog says hotspots are affected by sunlight and are invisible at night, and the wiki adds that they need illumination [3][4]. The Ore nodes wiki page is marked "Updated: A Long Time Ago", so current behaviour was not confirmed beyond these statements [4].

**Tool tiers.** Tools split into starter tools (Rock, Stone Hatchet, Stone Pickaxe, no workbench), Level 1 metal tools (Hatchet, Pickaxe), Level 2 salvaged tools (Salvaged Axe, Salvaged Icepick, Chainsaw) and the non-craftable Jackhammer [5][6][7][8][9][10][11][12][13]. Within the wiki's gather columns, each tier's Gather Damage figure is higher than the previous tier for its target, for example ore 5, 16, 30 and 50 for Rock, Stone Pickaxe, Pickaxe and Salvaged Icepick [5][7][9][11].

**Specialisation.** Per the wiki tables, hatchet-class tools list a Tree target, pickaxe-class tools list an Ore target, and the Rock lists both [5][6][7][8][9][10][11]. The wiki's Stone Pickaxe description says it harvests stone, metal ore and sulfur ore, but its table lists only one "Ore" row [5].

**Gather columns.** Each target row carries Gather Damage, Bonus and Condition Loss [5]. In every row opened, Bonus is one fifth of Gather Damage on Ore rows and one tenth on Tree and Flesh rows (for example Pickaxe ore 30 and 6, Hatchet tree 30 and 3) [5][7][8][9][11]. The wiki does not say what Bonus is, so its meaning is not asserted here.

**Fuel tools.** The Chainsaw requires Low Grade Fuel to run; no consumption rate is listed [12]. The Jackhammer's description says it can be refilled at a Workbench; no fuel figure is listed [13].

**Recycling tools.** Tools can be recycled: the Hatchet returns 60 Wood and 45 Metal Fragments at a Recycler and 40 Wood and 30 Metal Fragments at a Safe Zone Recycler [8]. Recyclers returned 100% of each listed output on the item pages [8]. The Recycler wiki page gives 60% yield at 5 seconds per item at monuments; the Safe Zone Recycler page gives 40% at 8 seconds per item at Outpost and Bandit [14][15]. Power Trip changed green recyclers to 50% by default, 60% with sufficient Power Plant power, with the cycle shortening from 5 s to 4.5 s at maximum power, and added a 75% red recycler [2]. Yellow recyclers were unchanged [2].

**Quarry.** The Mining Quarry wiki page says the item is admin-only and not available in normal gameplay; it lists no fuel or yield [19].

**Livestock.** The 1 October 2026 update lets livestock be harvested for meat, bones and leather like other animals, and sheep for wool [1].

text:
**Judgement layer.**

## Guidance 1 — Do not quote tool efficiency as resources per hit

- **Guidance:** Compare tools by tier and the wiki's figures only as relative indicators, and test yields in game.
- **Evidence basis:** The wiki gives undefined Gather Damage and Bonus columns and Facepunch gives no per-hit yield [3][5][9].
- **Confidence:** Medium. The absence of a per-hit figure is established from pages opened, not proved globally.
- **So what:** Treat any "N wood per hit" claim as unverified unless it shows its build and method.

## Guidance 2 — Learn the hotspot rhythm before upgrading tools

- **Guidance:** Practise chaining hotspot hits, since the bonus can reach 300% per hit on the same node.
- **Evidence basis:** Devblog 170 and the Ore nodes page state 150% rising to 300%, with a miss resetting it [3][4].
- **Confidence:** Medium. The mechanism is primary, but the page is old and the benefit in practice is inferred.
- **So what:** Good aim shortens each node visit, which reduces exposure time at open nodes.

## Guidance 3 — Check which recycler colour you are using

- **Guidance:** Compare recycler efficiency before dumping valuable items, and expect powered Power Plant machines to differ from the rest.
- **Evidence basis:** Power Trip lists 50%, 60% and 75% tiers, while wiki pages list 60% and 40% [2][14][15].
- **Confidence:** Medium. The update is primary, but the on-screen display and current state were not verified in game.
- **So what:** Recycle at the best available machine, and re-read the update notes after each patch.

title: Rust Weapons and Ammunition

text:
This deep-dive goes below the weapons overview in rust-items-crafting-foundation. It lists the main ranged weapons and ammunition types, the workbench level each needs, and the headline stats published on the Facepunch Rust Wiki item pages: craft cost, research cost, damage per ammo type, projectile velocity and headshot multiplier. It does not cover melee, explosives or the combat damage model, which belong to sibling documents.

The headline pattern is a tier ladder. Bows, the crossbow, the Waterpipe Shotgun and the Revolver need no more than Workbench Level 1; the Pump Shotgun, Thompson, Semi-Automatic Pistol and Python need Level 2; the Assault Rifle and Bolt Action Rifle need Level 3 [3][7][8][9][10][11][12][13][16][17]. Confidence is Medium: the numbers come from first-party wiki pages, but those pages carry no build date, and the Livestock Update (1 October 2026) lists no ammo or weapon damage changes [1].
title: Rust Weapons and Ammunition

text:
- Craftable firearms are gated by workbench level: Level 1 for the Revolver, Waterpipe Shotgun and Crossbow; Level 2 for the Pump Shotgun, Thompson, Semi-Automatic Pistol and Python; Level 3 for the Assault Rifle and Bolt Action Rifle [3][7][8][9][10][11][12][13][17].
- Ammo is gated too: Pistol Bullet needs Workbench Level 1, 5.56 Rifle Ammo and 12 Gauge Buckshot Level 2, HV and Explosive 5.56 Level 3 [4][5][6][19][20].
- Wiki-listed base damage per round: Assault Rifle 50, Bolt Action Rifle 80, Thompson 37.5, Python 55, Revolver 35, all with plain ammo of the matching family [3][13][12][8][7].
- Headshot multiplier is x2 for rifle and pistol rounds, x1.2 for buckshot, and x1.5 for arrows [3][7][10][16].
- The wiki shows two research routes per item: a Research Table price and a higher Workbench tech-tree price. The Assault Rifle shows 120 Scrap and 500 Scrap [3].
- The M249 is listed as not craftable, with Helicopter Crate and Bradley Crate drops [15]. The LR-300 page marks it neither craftable nor researchable [14].
- Livestock (1 October 2026) mentions only fixes touching the Crossbow, Minigun and similar items, with no stat changes [1].
title: Rust Weapons and Ammunition

text: Covers vanilla PC Rust firearms, bows and the ammunition they use, with workbench tier, craft and research cost and per-ammo damage as listed on Facepunch wiki item pages. Excludes melee weapons, explosives and launchers (see rust-raiding-costs-defence), the damage and armour model (see rust-combat-damage-model), weapon attachments beyond brief mention, server convars (see rust-server-convars-reference) and plugin changes (see rust-plugin-development-hooks). Checked against the Livestock Update of 1 October 2026 [1]. Not every weapon is covered: SMG variants, the SKS, M39, Minigun, HMLMG, L96 and flare or event weapons appear only where an ammo page lists them.
title: Rust Weapons and Ammunition

text:
- **Ammo family** — the ammunition group a weapon accepts: 5.56 Rifle, Pistol, 12 Gauge, Arrow [4][19][20][16].
- **Workbench level** — the tier needed to craft an item (see rust-items-crafting-foundation).
- **Tech tree price** — the Scrap cost of unlocking a recipe at a workbench, listed separately from the Research Table price [3].
- **Headshot multiplier** — the wiki column showing damage scaling on a head hit [3].
- **Velocity** — projectile speed in the wiki's units; drops with range for standard rounds [4].
title: Rust Weapons and Ammunition

text:
**Evidence layer.**

**Ammo families.** Each weapon accepts a fixed family. Rifle-calibre weapons take 5.56 Rifle Ammo in four variants: standard, HV, Explosive and Incendiary [3][13]. Pistol-calibre weapons (Revolver, Python, Semi-Automatic Pistol, Thompson) take Pistol Bullet, HV Pistol Ammo and Incendiary Pistol Bullet [7][8][9][12]. Shotguns take 12 Gauge Slug, Buckshot, Incendiary Shell and Handmade Shell [10][11]. Bows and the crossbow share Wooden, Bone, Fire and High Velocity arrows [16][17].

**Variant behaviour.** The wiki describes standard rifle and pistol ammo as losing velocity over distance with slightly reduced damage [4][19]. HV rifle ammo is described as faster, with less drop and slightly higher damage at long range [5]. Explosive rifle ammo explodes on contact for a small amount of fragmentation damage to nearby objects [6]. Per the Assault Rifle page, Incendiary 5.56 lists higher damage (56 versus 50) but lower velocity (225 versus 375), while Explosive lists the same damage as standard with lower velocity [3].

**Workbench gating.** Weapons list a required workbench level, and a higher bench shortens craft time: the Python takes 30 s at Level 2 and 15 s at Level 3 [8]; the Revolver takes 30 s, 15 s and 7 s at Levels 1, 2 and 3 [7].

**Two research prices.** Each item page lists a Research Table price and a "Tech Tree" price at its workbench. For the Revolver these are 30 and 125 Scrap [7]; for the Python 60 and 250 [8]; for the Bolt Action Rifle 120 and 500 [13]. The hunting bow, crossbow and wooden arrow pages state the recipe is known by default, so research is only needed for a physical blueprint for the Industrial Crafter [16][17][18].

**Loot-only weapons.** The M249 page lists the weapon as not craftable and not researchable, with loot from Helicopter and Bradley crates [15]. The LR-300 page lists no craft or research data [14].

text:
**Judgement layer.**

## Guidance 1 — Treat Workbench Level 2 as the practical firearm threshold

- **Guidance:** For most players, aim for Workbench Level 2 first; it unlocks the Python, Semi-Automatic Pistol, Thompson, Pump Shotgun and the standard 5.56 and shotgun ammo.
- **Evidence basis:** Those items and ammo list Level 2 [4][8][9][10][12][20].
- **Confidence:** Medium. The gating is cited, but "practical" is a judgement about value.
- **So what:** Budget the Basic Blueprint Fragments for Level 2 before chasing rifle research [2].

## Guidance 2 — Do not buy rifle research before checking the ammo bench

- **Guidance:** Confirm you can craft the matching ammo at your bench level before paying for a rifle.
- **Evidence basis:** The Assault Rifle and Bolt Action Rifle need Level 3, while standard 5.56 needs Level 2 and HV or Explosive needs Level 3 [3][4][5][6][13].
- **Confidence:** Medium. Costs are first-party but undated.
- **So what:** A Level 3 rifle with no ammo supply is a poor spend of Scrap.

## Guidance 3 — Recheck every number after each first-Thursday update

- **Guidance:** Treat all figures here as a snapshot and re-verify in game before building a loadout or server economy.
- **Evidence basis:** Wiki pages carry no build stamp and Meta Shift changed ammo stat display [2][3].
- **Confidence:** Medium. Staleness risk is inferred, not shown.
- **So what:** Cite figures with a date and the Livestock build.

title: Rust Carbon versus Oxide

text:
This document compares the two live Rust server frameworks, Oxide (uMod) and Carbon, on licence, installation, Oxide-plugin compatibility, performance claims, tags, maintenance status and release cadence. It goes deeper than the foundation document and uses only first-party pages: project sites, GitHub repositories, the GitHub release and repository APIs, and the Facepunch wiki.

Headline findings as of 2026-10-08: both repositories are unarchived and were pushed to within the last day or so of the check [11][12]; Oxide.Rust is MIT-licensed and Carbon's repository is GPL-3.0, although Carbon's own website says MIT [1][3][6][14]; all performance and compatibility advantages are vendor claims with no benchmark on any page opened [1][3][9]. Confidence is Medium: facts are primary-sourced, but Oxide's own install guide could not be opened and no independent benchmark exists in the sources.
title: Rust Carbon versus Oxide

text:
- Oxide.Rust's repository licence is MIT (GitHub API spdx id MIT) [6][12]. Carbon's repository licence is GPL-3.0 (API and LICENSE file) [1][11][14].
- Carbon's website says "Released under the MIT License", which contradicts the repository's GPL-3.0 licence file; this is unresolved [3][14].
- The two cannot run on the same install: Oxide ships pre-patched Facepunch DLLs while Carbon patches DLLs at runtime, so vanilla DLLs must be restored before migrating [5].
- Carbon's migration page says Oxide `o.` commands become `c.`, and that config, data, lang and user/group files are copied automatically on first start [5].
- Oxide shipped 12 releases between 2026-08-28 and 2026-10-07 (the 12 newest returned by the API) and several are labelled as patches for named Rust updates or hotfixes [7].
- Carbon's README says its production build "gets updated twice times a month" (vendor claim); its release list holds one rolling production tag, published 2026-10-02 [1][2].
- Facepunch's wiki lists `Oxide` (code `o`) and `Carbon` (code `y`) as separate server browser tags [10].
- No opened page contains a measured benchmark comparing the two *(assessed: absence of evidence in these sources only)* [1][3][9].
title: Rust Carbon versus Oxide

text: Covered: Oxide.Rust and Carbon on PC Rust dedicated servers, as of Rust's Livestock update (1 Oct 2026) and the framework versions named above. Not covered: plugin development (see rust-plugin-development-hooks), individual plugins, permission command syntax (see rust-modding-plugins-foundation), console, client-side modding. Install steps are summarised from the pages that could be opened; Oxide's own install guide URL returned 404.
title: Rust Carbon versus Oxide

text:
- **Oxide / uMod:** the long-running Rust modding framework; the Oxide.Rust repository is the "Rust game extension for the Oxide modding framework" [6].
- **Carbon:** an alternative framework describing itself as a drop-in Oxide replacement [3].
- **Harmony:** the C# runtime patching library both frameworks list as supported (Harmony 2.0) [5].
- **Dynamic hook loading:** Carbon's stated behaviour of activating only the hooks plugins use [3][5].
- **Rolling release tag:** a GitHub release whose tag name stays fixed (for example `production_build`) while its contents are replaced, so tag history does not show cadence [2].
title: Rust Carbon versus Oxide

text:
**Installation, Oxide.** Per the Facepunch wiki: download the latest Oxide installer from the Oxide website, stop the server, run the installer, start the server; the `oxide` console command then opens the Oxide console where plugins and Oxide updates are managed [8]. Oxide's documentation home points to Server Owners and Core Documentation sections, but this check did not read an install guide [13].

**Installation, Carbon (Windows).** Download `Carbon.Windows.TARGET.zip` from the GitHub Releases page, extract it to the server root containing `RustDedicated.exe` keeping the folder structure and overwriting as needed, then start the server; TARGET is Release or Debug depending on the build branch [4]. The page asks that server files be verified and the server kept up to date at every boot [4]. The repository also mentions a quick-start script for Windows and Linux [1]. Linux and OSX tabs exist but their content was not captured [4].

**Compatibility.** Carbon states it is fully compatible with Oxide and keeps the folder and plugin structure [1][3]. Its porting page states the two cannot coexist, that Oxide's pre-patched DLLs must be replaced with vanilla ones through a SteamCMD `validate` before Carbon is extracted, and that both use Harmony 2.0 [5]. The Facepunch wiki's Carbon page repeats that Oxide plugins run without extra patches, but the page is undated ("Updated: A Long Time Ago") and carries no version numbers [9].

**Performance claims (vendor claims, not measurements).** Carbon's site says performance is "the number one factor", hooks load dynamically so only used hooks are active, and only essential hooks are provided [3]. The README says it uses the latest C# and Harmony "for the best performance and stability possible" [1]. The Facepunch wiki Carbon page claims Harmony micro-optimisations reduce CPU overhead and memory allocations [9]. None of these pages gives a benchmark or measured result [1][3][9]. No comparable performance claim for Oxide was found on the pages opened [6][8][13].

**Features Carbon claims over Oxide.** Carbon's porting page tabulates dynamic patching, self-updating, remote hook updates on boot, a built-in profiler, SQLite permissions and "regular updates" as Carbon-only, with Harmony 2.0 and "regularly maintained" shared [5]. This table is Carbon's own, so the Oxide column is a competitor's statement; the "regular updates" row is contradicted for Oxide by its release history below [5][7].

text:
- Observed Oxide cadence: the 12 newest releases span 2026-08-28 (2.0.7638) to 2026-10-07 (2.0.7810), about 40 days, including 2.0.7676 (3 Sept, patching a September 3rd Rust update), 2.0.7716 (11 Sept), 2.0.7723 (17 Sept), 2.0.7726 (22 Sept), 2.0.7783 (1 Oct) and 2.0.7801 (2 Oct) [7]. Several release bodies name the Rust update or hotfix they patch, so Oxide ships a framework release to follow Rust updates [7].
- Observed Carbon cadence: the release list holds rolling tags (`production_build`, `edge_build`, `experimental_build`, `rustbeta_*`), so release frequency cannot be read from the tags; the experimental build was last published 2026-08-22 and aux01 on 2026-09-15 [2]. The README's "twice times a month" production cadence is a claim and was not verified against history [1]. The list returned was truncated after six releases, so more may exist [2].
- Carbon's production release (2 Oct) and Oxide's patches (1-2 Oct) both landed within a day or two of the Livestock update of 1 Oct 2026 [2][7]; Carbon's production body does not state a Rust build in the data read, unlike Oxide's [2][7].
- Volatile: every version number in this document changes at least monthly; re-check before relying on it.

Framework updates follow Rust releases tracked in rust-update-timeline-2026 and rust-updates-meta-foundation. New Rust systems gain hooks through framework releases; for example Oxide 2.0.7783 added livestock and growable-entity hooks after the 1 October update, relevant to rust-farming-food [7]. text:
## Guidance 1 — Decide on licence obligations from the repository, not the website

- **Guidance:** If you redistribute or modify framework code, treat Carbon as GPL-3.0 (the repository and LICENSE file) and Oxide.Rust as MIT, and ask the Carbon maintainers about the website's MIT statement.
- **Evidence basis:** Repository API and LICENSE file versus website text [3][11][12][14].
- **Confidence:** Medium. The sources conflict and this document is not legal advice.
- **So what:** Hosting plugins on a server rarely involves redistributing the framework, but anyone bundling or forking it should resolve the conflict first.

## Guidance 2 — Treat performance claims as untested until measured on your own server

- **Guidance:** Do not choose Carbon for speed on the strength of its pages; run both on a staging copy of your plugin set and compare server frame time and memory.
- **Evidence basis:** Only vendor statements, with no benchmark in the opened pages [1][3][9].
- **Confidence:** Medium. The absence of benchmarks in the sources read is verifiable, but a benchmark may exist elsewhere.
- **So what:** Avoid a migration justified only by marketing copy.

## Guidance 3 — Plan migration as a rehearsed change with a rollback

- **Guidance:** Back up the server, rehearse the Oxide-to-Carbon move, keep the Oxide install copy, and update scripts from `o.` to `c.`.
- **Evidence basis:** Porting page steps and no-coexistence statement [5].
- **Confidence:** Medium. The steps are first-party, but the rollback advice is inference.
- **So what:** A failed first start leaves you able to restore the previous state before wipe day.

## Guidance 4 — Gate Rust updates on the framework release in either case

- **Guidance:** After each monthly Rust update, wait for the matching framework release (Oxide notes name the Rust update; for Carbon check the production build date) before updating the live server.
- **Evidence basis:** Oxide release notes naming Rust updates [7]; Carbon's production release dated within a day of Livestock [2].
- **Confidence:** Medium. Two observed release windows only.
- **So what:** Fewer broken hooks after a wipe-day update.

text:
Rust servers are modded through third-party frameworks that load C# plugins. The two live frameworks are Oxide (the uMod project, MIT licensed) and Carbon (GPL-3.0, billed as a drop-in Oxide replacement) [1][3][5]. Both were actively releasing on 2026-10-08: Oxide.Rust tag 2.0.7810 on 2026-10-07 and Carbon "Production Build v2.0.262" on 2026-10-02 [2][4].

This document covers what each framework is, how they differ, installation and the permission model, plugin sources and monetisation, and how the Rust server browser classifies modded servers. Confidence is Medium: framework status is primary-sourced, but the uMod licence rules, any explicit Facepunch policy on modded servers and the Oxide install guide pages could not be opened, so those parts rest on indirect sources or are flagged as open questions.

text:
- Oxide.Rust is a public GitHub repository under the MIT licence, with active development on the `develop` branch [3]. Its newest release seen was tag 2.0.7810, published 2026-10-07 [4].
- An earlier Oxide.Rust release, 2.0.7801 (2026-10-02), is described as a patch for the "October 2nd Rust hotfix #3 (2634.289.1)" [4].
- Carbon is a mod loader built on C# and Harmony with a permission system, user system and in-game GUI, licensed GPL-3.0 [1]. Its latest release seen was "Production Build v2.0.262", published 2026-10-02 [2].
- Carbon states it is fully compatible with Oxide plugins and keeps the same folder and plugin structure [1][5].
- Carbon maps its branches to Rust branches: `main` to public, `experimental` usually to release, `production` to public (or release on wipe day), with staging and aux branches described as extremely unstable [1].
- The Facepunch wiki lists `Modded`, `Oxide` and `Carbon` as server browser tags set through the `server.tags` convar [8].
- Codefling is a marketplace listing many paid Rust plugins, plus maps, prefabs and tools; some plugins are free [12].

text:
- **Oxide / uMod:** the long-standing Rust modding framework; its docs are at docs.oxidemod.com [7][10].
- **Carbon:** an alternative mod loader, self-updating, using Harmony [1].
- **Plugin:** a C# file placed in the framework's plugins folder (`oxide/plugins` for Oxide) [7].
- **Permission:** a dotted string such as `coolplugin.use` granted to users or groups [11].
- **Server browser tag:** a short code set in `server.tags`; Modded, Oxide and Carbon are compressed to `z`, `o`, `y` [8].
title: Rust Modding and Plugins: Foundation

text:
**Frameworks.** Oxide is described by the Facepunch wiki as a modding framework letting owners install plugins that change gameplay, such as items, crafting recipes and player behaviour [7]. Carbon describes itself as a self-updating, lightweight mod loader using the latest C# and Harmony, with a permission system, user system and in-game GUI [1].

**Differences (Carbon's own claims).** Carbon says it provides only essential hooks so a server stays close to vanilla, loads only hooks that plugins use, supports hot reload of Harmony mods, has SQL permissions with custom serializers, and an in-game interface for installing and updating plugins [5]. These are vendor claims, not independent benchmarks.

**Installation overview.** Oxide: per the Facepunch wiki, stop the server, run the Oxide installer from the Oxide site, and restart; typing `oxide` in the server console reaches the Oxide console [7]. Oxide's docs home lists dedicated guides for Server Setup, Installing Oxide, Installing Plugins and Permissions [10]. Carbon: download the platform archive from GitHub Releases, extract it to the root of the Rust dedicated server (beside `RustDedicated.exe` on Windows), start the server, and keep server files updated and verified [2][6]. A QuickStart script for Windows and Linux also exists [1].

**Plugin installation.** Plugins are downloaded from the Oxide site or community sites and placed in the `oxide/plugins` folder [7]. Carbon states the same folder structure is retained [5].

**Permissions model.** A practitioner guide documents that uMod creates two groups automatically, `admin` and `default`, that users can be in several groups, and that group permissions supersede individual grants [11]. Each plugin defines its own permission names, so the plugin author's setup notes are authoritative [11].

text:
## Guidance 1 — Pick the framework by plugin set and licence, not by speed claims

- **Guidance:** Choose Oxide when you rely on the broad uMod ecosystem and want the MIT-licensed reference implementation; consider Carbon for its in-game GUI and branch tracking after testing your plugin set on a staging server.
- **Evidence basis:** Both are active and Oxide-plugin-compatible per the vendor [1][2][3][4][5].
- **Confidence:** Medium. Compatibility and performance claims come from Carbon's own pages, not independent tests.
- **So what:** Do not migrate a live wipe server without rehearsing every plugin.

## Guidance 2 — Check the framework release before updating Rust

- **Guidance:** Check the framework's latest release for the new Rust build before updating the game server, and expect hook breakage after big updates.
- **Evidence basis:** Oxide shipped a dedicated patch for a Rust hotfix [4]; Carbon ties branches to Rust branches [1].
- **Confidence:** Medium. Based on two observed release histories.
- **So what:** Schedule updates after the framework release and keep a rollback copy.

## Guidance 3 — Grant plugin permissions to groups, not individuals

- **Guidance:** Manage access through groups with parent inheritance, since group permissions supersede individual grants.
- **Evidence basis:** Practitioner guide on groups and precedence [11].
- **Confidence:** Medium. A single practitioner source, so it cannot exceed Medium.
- **So what:** Fewer stale per-player grants and easier audits.

## Guidance 4 — Read the licence on every paid plugin before buying

- **Guidance:** Treat the marketplace front page as not stating licence terms and ask the author about multi-server use and redistribution.
- **Evidence basis:** Codefling's front page gave no licence terms [12].
- **Confidence:** Low. Absence of terms on one page is weak evidence about the whole marketplace.
- **So what:** Avoid unintended licence breaches when running several servers.
